INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — MOCK EXAM #7
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. How can flashcards help with vocabulary? (1 mark)
   A. They let you practise a word and its meaning again and again
   B. They cost a lot
   C. They make words disappear
   D. They replace reading

2. What can a weather forecast tell us? (1 mark)
   A. How old we are
   B. What the weather will be like
   C. Who will win a race
   D. What we will eat

3. Which sentence gives information but not an instruction? (1 mark)
   A. Today the sky is cloudy.
   B. Bring the clothes.
   C. Stay indoors.
   D. Close the window.

4. Which sentence should be read with a rising voice in English? (1 mark)
   A. Are you coming to school?
   B. You are coming to school.
   C. We go to school.
   D. Come to school.

5. In English, what usually happens to the voice at the end of a question? (1 mark)
   A. It falls to silence
   B. It rises
   C. It becomes a whisper
   D. It stays exactly the same always

6. Which word needs a capital letter? (1 mark)
   A. market
   B. road
   C. Nairobi
   D. river

7. How many full stops are needed in: The sky is dark. Rain is coming. (1 mark)
   A. One
   B. Two
   C. Three
   D. None

8. Which sentence has the punctuation of a list correct? (1 mark)
   A. We wore, hats scarves and coats.
   B. We wore hats scarves and coats.
   C. We wore hats, scarves and coats.
   D. We wore hats scarves, and coats

9. Which is a verb in: The pot tipped over? (1 mark)
   A. over
   B. tipped
   C. pot
   D. The

10. What does Many hands make light work mean? (1 mark)
   A. Hands are light
   B. Work is easier when people share it
   C. Work is always easy
   D. Nobody should help

11. What does Honesty is the best policy teach? (1 mark)
   A. Only rich people are honest
   B. Truth is unimportant
   C. Lying is fine
   D. Telling the truth is the wisest choice

12. What does the proverb Look before you leap advise a writer of a story about a careless pupil? (1 mark)
   A. Think before acting
   B. Run fast
   C. Be careless
   D. Never look

13. What should you do if a classmate's story is not as good as yours? (1 mark)
   A. Listen politely and give kind feedback
   B. Leave
   C. Laugh at them
   D. Interrupt

14. What kind of word is when in When I arrived, the shop was closed? (1 mark)
   A. A conjunction
   B. An adjective
   C. A number
   D. A noun

15. Why do we check a dictionary meaning against the sentence? (1 mark)
   A. Sentences have no meaning
   B. Words can have more than one meaning
   C. Dictionaries are wrong
   D. Words never change

16. What should you keep in mind when scanning? (1 mark)
   A. A song
   B. Nothing
   C. What you are looking for
   D. A poem

17. What is a bargain? (1 mark)
   A. To steal
   B. To discuss the price
   C. To sleep
   D. To run

18. What is a hobby? (1 mark)
   A. A test
   B. A punishment
   C. A school rule
   D. Something you enjoy doing regularly in your free time

19. Which is a constructive leisure activity? (1 mark)
   A. Wasting money
   B. Reading a book
   C. Fighting
   D. Harming others

20. How should notes be written? (1 mark)
   A. As long sentences
   B. As whole paragraphs
   C. As drawings only
   D. As short phrases of key words

21. Which interjection shows praise? (1 mark)
   A. Oops
   B. Ouch
   C. Yuck
   D. Bravo

22. What is the main idea of a passage? (1 mark)
   A. The date
   B. What it is mostly about
   C. The page number
   D. The last word

23. What should a dialogue about leisure show? (1 mark)
   A. Good values such as responsibility
   B. Unkindness
   C. Rudeness
   D. Bad habits

24. A good dialogue should have (1 mark)
   A. no words
   B. only one word
   C. no characters
   D. an ending

25. Why do writers use interjections in dialogues? (1 mark)
   A. To show feelings and make speech natural
   B. To make it longer
   C. To hide the story
   D. To fill the page

26. What is a call centre? (1 mark)
   A. A school
   B. A farm
   C. A place where staff answer customers' phone calls
   D. A market

27. What is a digital device? (1 mark)
   A. A wooden tool
   B. A type of song
   C. A kind of fruit
   D. A machine that works with electronic signals to help us communicate or work

28. Why should you ask an adult before giving your address on an online form? (1 mark)
   A. To stay safe
   B. No reason
   C. To waste time
   D. To make it longer

29. What should a real-life experience description include? (1 mark)
   A. Nothing
   B. Who, what, when, where and how you felt
   C. Only a number
   D. Only a title

30. Which is a poor instruction? (1 mark)
   A. Do the thing with the papers
   B. Wet your hands
   C. Rinse the soap
   D. Collect the exercise books and place them on the table

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Explain why you should not share personal details on a form without asking an adult. (3 marks)

32. Give two features of a poem. (2 marks)

33. Give three questions you can ask when studying a picture. (3 marks)

34. Name two prepositions used to show position. (2 marks)

35. Name two elements of a story. (2 marks)

36. Write a short paragraph of three sentences about why we should write neatly. Check your capital letters and full stops. (5 marks)

37. Give two adjectives to describe a mobile phone. (2 marks)

38. Write one instruction from the road safety dialogue. (2 marks)

39. Write two polite phrases to interrupt. (2 marks)

40. Give the plural of each English noun: cabbage, onion. (2 marks)

41. Describe how you would play Simon says with your class and say what it teaches. (5 marks)

42. Copy this sentence correctly: the food is hot (2 marks)

43. Compose a four-line poem about leisure that includes two interjections. (5 marks)

44. List three polite expressions used during a telephone call. (3 marks)

45. State three steps for reading your part in a dialogue. (3 marks)

46. Put the steps in order: (a) Finally, serve. (b) First, boil water. (c) Next, add tea leaves. (3 marks)

47. Give two sequence words. (2 marks)

48. List the two verbs in the sentence: The teacher counted the votes and announced the winner. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — MOCK EXAM #7 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — They let you practise a word and its meaning again and again
   Flashcards are a simple tool for revision.

2. B — What the weather will be like
   A forecast predicts the weather.

3. A — Today the sky is cloudy.
   It only tells about the weather.

4. A — Are you coming to school?
   It is a question.

5. B — It rises
   Many questions end with a rising voice.

6. C — Nairobi
   Names of towns begin with capital letters.

7. B — Two
   There are two sentences, so two full stops.

8. C — We wore hats, scarves and coats.
   A comma follows each item except the last two, which are joined by and.

9. B — tipped
   Tipped shows what the pot did.

10. B — Work is easier when people share it
   It is a proverb about working together.

11. D — Telling the truth is the wisest choice
   It praises honesty.

12. A — Think before acting
   It would fit a story where carelessness causes trouble.

13. A — Listen politely and give kind feedback
   Respect is important.

14. A — A conjunction
   When joins two ideas by time.

15. B — Words can have more than one meaning
   The right meaning depends on context.

16. C — What you are looking for
   Scanning needs a target.

17. B — To discuss the price
   Bargaining is agreeing on price.

18. D — Something you enjoy doing regularly in your free time
   A hobby is a regular enjoyable activity.

19. B — Reading a book
   Constructive activities build people up.

20. D — As short phrases of key words
   Notes are brief.

21. D — Bravo
   Bravo praises good work.

22. B — What it is mostly about
   The main idea is the central point.

23. A — Good values such as responsibility
   Dialogues can teach values.

24. D — an ending
   Every piece needs an ending.

25. A — To show feelings and make speech natural
   Interjections show emotions.

26. C — A place where staff answer customers' phone calls
   Call centre staff answer calls.

27. D — A machine that works with electronic signals to help us communicate or work
   Phones and computers are digital devices.

28. A — To stay safe
   Personal details should be protected.

29. B — Who, what, when, where and how you felt
   These details make it clear.

30. A — Do the thing with the papers
   It is vague.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: Someone could misuse the details, so a trusted adult should check that it is safe.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the risk, one for asking an adult, one for a clear explanation.

32. (2 marks)
   Answer: Short lines, stanzas, rhyme, rhythm, images (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: Who is there, where are they, what are they doing, why, what happens next.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: on, in, under, behind, beside, between, in front of, outside (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

35. (2 marks)
   Answer: Title, characters, setting, problem, events, ending (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

36. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any three neat, complete sentences, for example Neat writing helps others to read my work. It shows respect for the reader. I feel proud when my book is tidy.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct sentence, one mark for capital letters and one for full stops.

37. (2 marks)
   Answer: small, black, thin, new, flat (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each sensible adjective.

38. (2 marks)
   Answer: Look right, then left, then right again. (or Cross at a zebra crossing.)
   Working / marking points: One mark for a correct instruction and one for a complete sentence.

39. (2 marks)
   Answer: Excuse me, may I say something? Sorry to interrupt, but could you repeat that?
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

40. (2 marks)
   Answer: cabbages, onions
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct plural.

41. (5 marks)
   Answer: One pupil is the leader. The leader gives instructions. Pupils obey only when the leader says Simon says. Those who obey a wrong instruction are out. The game teaches careful listening.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the leader, one for the rule, one for what happens when a player breaks the rule, and two marks for explaining what it teaches.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: The food is hot.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the capital letter and one mark for the full stop.

43. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any four lines about free time with two suitable interjections, for example Wow, it is time to play! Hurray, no lessons today! We run and read and sing, Free time is a lovely thing.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each line up to four and one mark for two suitable interjections.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Good morning, please, thank you, excuse me, goodbye, may I speak to (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Read silently first, underline your lines, practise them, watch the punctuation, wait for your cue.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each step.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: b, c, a
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct position.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: first, next, then, finally (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark each.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: counted, announced
   Working / marking points: One mark for each verb. Teacher, votes and winner are nouns.
